song.title: Feels Like We Only Go Backwards

guitar.evidence: Kevin Parker (essentially a one-man studio project) uses various vintage and boutique guitars (Eastwood, Höfner) but has no single iconic signature instrument.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown with low confidence given his varied, non-iconic gear choices.

tone.target: warbly lo-fi psychedelic clean with tape wobble
tone.profile: warbly lo-fi psychedelic clean with tape wobble
tone.summary: A warm, modulated signal chain using light compression and a clean Fender-style amp (US Deluxe) combined with Chorus for wobble, Tape delay, and subtle Fuzz for lo-fi haze.

rig.name: Tame Impala - Feels Like We Only Go Backwards - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide slight compression for a smooth, sustained clean tone.
Introduce a subtle, warm fuzz haze for lo-fi texture.
blocks.gap: The Fuzz model is generally aggressive; settings must be kept very low to achieve 'soft fuzz' as requested.

alternatives.reason: If the Fuzz sounds too harsh, Red Haze could provide a gentler grit.

blocks.gap: The source material does not require a wah effect.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a clean Fender/JC style amp for the required warm, non-aggressive tone.
Provide a bright, open sound suitable for clean psychedelic tones.
Create the required 'wobbly modulation' and psychedelic shimmer.
Simulate the 'tape-like delay' with moderate feedback.
blocks.gap: While Tape is available, Digital Delay offers more precise control for a controlled lo-fi echo effect.

alternatives.reason: If the desired sound is purely analog and warm, use Tape instead of Digital Delay.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle ambience without the 'big hall reverb' specified in the avoidance list.

improvements.summary: Improve the cabinet realism by swapping the current IR for a warmer, more vintage-sounding option to better match the lo-fi psychedelic tone.

proposals.reason: The current bright US 2x12 is too pristine; a warmer, vintage IR will enhance the lo-fi haze.
